theme: Expedia and Hotels.com datasets (Expedia hotel recommendation Kaggle, personalized ranking ICDM 2013, Expedia scrapers), Trivago RecSys 2019, Kayak/Skyscanner scrapers
notes: WebSearch tool exhausted its session-wide quota (200/200, shared across all concurrent scouts) before I could run any query with it, so this scout ran entirely on WebFetch: (1) attempted Bing and DuckDuckGo HTML search pages -- Bing returned no useful GitHub links, DuckDuckGo HTML served a CAPTCHA and could not be read; (2) fell back to github.com native search and github.com/topics/<tag> pages fetched directly, which worked until GitHub itself began returning HTTP 429 (rate limited, presumably from many concurrent scouts hitting github.com even though gh CLI was avoided as instructed) partway through -- several planned queries (site-search for 'expedia-hotel-recommendations', ICDM2013 Kaggle mirrors specifically, hotels.com more broadly, Kayak/Skyscanner with 'dataset' rather than 'scraper') returned 429 and were not retried to avoid worsening the shared limit. Net effect: coverage of the Trivago RecSys 2019 ecosystem is solid (official challenge repo + three independent competitor solution repos, none of which bundle the raw interaction logs -- all require pulling data from the trivago/RecSys2019 challenge site, which is outside our sanctioned-source list and would need a human ToS call). Coverage of Kaggle 'Expedia Hotel Recommendations' (2016) and the ICDM 2013 'Personalize Expedia Hotel Searches' dataset specifically is weaker -- I could not confirm a GitHub mirror that actually commits the raw CSVs (benhamner/expedia-personalized-sort, a name I expected from training-era memory, 404s; it may never have existed or was renamed/deleted). Every scraper repo found targets Expedia/Trivago/Hotels.com/Kayak web pages, none commit sample data, and per the rules I did not run any of them. None of these datasets carry ABNB-adjacent geography or STR-specific content -- they are hotel/OTA session-log and review data, so their fit is against gap #9 (competitor and adjacent supply/demand signal) and possibly #2 (realised ADR/occupancy proxies via hotel price session logs) rather than a close STR match. If another scout has WebSearch budget left, worth chasing: (a) a working GitHub mirror of the raw Expedia ICDM2013 / Kaggle-2016 CSVs (Kaggle enforces a ToU that discourages redistribution, so any GitHub copy is likely small/partial or an Apache-licensed loader only); (b) 'agoda scraper', 'booking.com scraper github' broader than what CONTEXT.md already lists; (c) archived Trivago RecSys 2019 dataset via Zenodo (recsyschallenge.com states data was later released via a Zenodo DOI for reproducibility after the competition -- worth checking directly, I could not search for it here).

candidates.name: recsyschallenge/2019
candidates.what_it_holds: Official ACM RecSys Challenge 2019 organizer repo (trivago + TU Wien + Politecnico di Milano + Karlsruhe Institute of Technology). data/ dir with dataset description docs, docs/ with problem definition and installation guides, src/ with a popularity baseline and submission-scoring/validation scripts. MIT licensed, 101 stars, 44 forks, 25 commits. The actual click-out session logs (hotel search sessions with impressions, filters, prices, clicks) are described here but distributed off-repo via the official challenge site/Zenodo, not committed as files in this repo.
candidates.why_useful: Trivago hotel-search session data (millions of search sessions with price/position/click) is a real-time OTA demand and price-sensitivity dataset -- useful as a competitor/adjacent-supply comparator (gap #9) and as a template for session-based demand modeling methodology (gap #17). Data itself needs pulling from the official host, which is outside sanctioned sources -- flag as pointer.
candidates.size_hint: millions of session-log rows (per challenge description); not stored in this repo, hosted externally
candidates.time_coverage: 2018 (RecSys Challenge 2019 used ~1 month of trivago click-out logs)
candidates.geography: Europe-weighted, trivago's session logs (global but skewed EU)
candidates.license: MIT (repo code); underlying data license set separately by trivago/challenge organizers
candidates.last_activity: unspecified exact date; repo is from the 2019 challenge, static since

candidates.name: logicai-io/recsys2019
candidates.what_it_holds: 1st-place winning solution to RecSys Challenge 2019 (trivago). cpp/ feature extraction, data/ dir, publications/, src/ Python pipelines; ships a download_data.sh script rather than committing the raw data itself; 37 LightGBM ranker models with ensemble blending. Apache-2.0, 94 stars, 15 forks, 238 commits.
candidates.why_useful: A working, documented one-command pull-and-featurize pipeline for the trivago click-out dataset (once obtained from the official host) plus a full feature-engineering reference for turning OTA session logs into demand/price-sensitivity features -- reusable methodology for gap #17 (nowcasting methods) even if the raw data pull itself needs a ToS decision.
candidates.last_activity: unspecified; static since 2019 challenge, last seen with 238 commits

candidates.name: rn5l/rsc19
candidates.what_it_holds: Another RecSys Challenge 2019 (trivago) competitor submission: preprocessing scripts, session-log transformation, latent-factor generation, LightGBM training. Requires user to extract a provided data zip into _data/raw manually -- no data committed, no license file visible.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent implementation of the trivago session-log pipeline; marginal beyond logicai-io's repo but confirms multiple independent codebases exist for the same dataset, increasing confidence the underlying data is recoverable if a human clears the ToS question.

candidates.name: rosetta-ai/rosetta_recsys2019
candidates.what_it_holds: 4th-place solution to RecSys Challenge 2019 by Team RosettaAI. Code and docs only (Neural Net / LightGBM / XGBoost models); README instructs placing unzipped official challenge data into an input/ directory -- no data files committed. Apache-2.0, 58 stars, 16 forks, 41 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Third independent trivago-challenge codebase; adds little beyond logicai-io but is a clean, well-documented modeling reference if the team ever gets the underlying session logs.

candidates.name: oxylabs/trivago-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Commercial scraper wrapper (Oxylabs) for pulling live Trivago hotel search-result pages: location, price, ratings, amenities, guest reviews, via Oxylabs' paid scraping API. Code-examples folder with sample requests in several languages and a JSON response schema; no data files committed. 33 stars, 1 fork, 13 commits, no license file visible.
candidates.why_useful: A live-price acquisition method for hotel ADR/occupancy proxies (gap #2) via a metasearch aggregator that indexes many OTAs including Airbnb-adjacent short-term-rental listings on some markets -- flagged as method only; requires a paid API key so not runnable under project rules without a human decision, and touches a live commercial site (ToS question).

candidates.name: factden/expedia-hotel-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apify actor (JavaScript) scraping Expedia Group brands (Expedia, Hotels.com, Orbitz, Travelocity, Wotif, CheapTickets, ebookers) for guest ratings, category sub-ratings, review text, and owner responses; outputs CSV/JSON via Apify's platform API. Updated Sep 7 2026 (active/maintained).
candidates.why_useful: Live acquisition path for competitor hotel review volume/sentiment across all 7 Expedia Group brands at once -- a broader, actively maintained alternative to the Booking.com 515k-review Kaggle set already held; review-count trend could serve as a rough competitor demand/engagement proxy (gap #9). Requires running against a live commercial site, so per project rules this is catalogued as method only and left unrun.
candidates.size_hint: n/a (scraper, no committed data; pulls arbitrary volume per run)

candidates.name: factden/hotels-com-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion Apify actor specifically for Hotels.com: guest ratings, category sub-ratings, review text, owner responses; no login/API key required per description; CSV/JSON/API output.
candidates.why_useful: Narrower duplicate of factden's Expedia-Group scraper focused on Hotels.com alone; same rationale (competitor engagement/demand proxy, gap #9), same caveats (live scrape, ToS question, no data committed).

candidates.name: omkarcloud/expedia-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Tool for searching airports, comparing flights and hotel fares, and retrieving real-time itineraries/booking links from Expedia; commercial product with a free tier (5,000 requests/month). Last updated 30 Apr 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Another live-pull path to Expedia pricing/availability, potentially usable for flight-side travel-demand cross-checks (gap #10 adjacency) as well as hotel ADR proxies; no data committed, requires running against a live commercial site.

candidates.name: oxylabs/expedia-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Java-based Expedia scraper (Oxylabs) pulling flights, prices, destinations, and hotel information from the live site. Commercial API wrapper, code examples only, no data committed. Last updated 22 Jun 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Third independent live-pull option for Expedia hotel/flight pricing; adds nothing over omkarcloud/expedia-scraper beyond language choice.

candidates.name: MeshalAlamr/flight-price-prediction
candidates.what_it_holds: Flight ticket price dataset scraped from Kayak, used for a random-forest price-prediction model; repo is a student/portfolio ML project with the scraped CSV committed alongside notebooks.
candidates.why_useful: Committed flight-price dataset scraped from Kayak could serve as a low-value cross-check on general travel-price/demand trends (peripheral to ABNB, closer to airline capacity gap #10), but scope and vintage are almost certainly narrow (single-route/date snapshot typical of these portfolio projects) -- worth a look only if airline-fare read-through becomes a workstream.
candidates.size_hint: unknown row count; likely a single-scrape CSV (typical of these student projects, probably hundreds to low thousands of rows)
candidates.geography: unspecified (Kayak search, likely a handful of routes)

candidates.name: thorwhalen/farepy
candidates.what_it_holds: Multi-source flight-search Python client with normalized results, caching, and batch support, including a Kayak integration alongside other flight-search backends.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose flight-fare pull tool; could feed an airfare/travel-cost proxy series (gap #10) if a team member wants time-series airfare tracking beyond BLS/FRED airfare CPI already held, but it is a live scraper/aggregator client, not a stored dataset.

candidates.name: skyscanner/skyscanner-python-sdk
candidates.what_it_holds: Official (now archived/deprecated) Python SDK for the Skyscanner Flights, Hotels, and Car Hire APIs. Archived read-only Jan 2026; deprecated by Skyscanner itself since May 2020 with a stated warning the API will stop working. Apache License, 125 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Historical interest only -- confirms Skyscanner once exposed a hotel-price API wrapped here, but the underlying API is dead and the SDK is explicitly non-functional against current endpoints. Not a usable acquisition method today.

candidates.name: FAHADPN/Hotel-search-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Small utility generating Kayak.co.in redirect/search-result links for hotel queries; not a scraper of structured data, just a URL-builder.
candidates.why_useful: Negligible research value -- flagged only for completeness; does not extract or store any pricing/availability data itself.
